sections.description: This section introduces the patient case, detailing the presenting symptoms, comprehensive medical history, and chronological timeline of prior cardiac interventions. It establishes the clinical context of a complex patient requiring multidisciplinary evaluation and highlights how the initial presentation prompted investigation into prosthetic valve dysfunction.
subtopics: Presenting symptoms: dyspnea, chest discomfort, dizziness, and fatigue in the context of known prosthetic valve history
Comprehensive past medical history: coronary artery disease with multiple PCIs, atrioventricular block with pacemaker, diabetes mellitus, COPD, and gastrointestinal bleeding
Timeline of aortic valve interventions: Lotus valve (2014), Evolut TAV-in-TAV (2022), and progression to third intervention
The episode of prosthetic valve endocarditis: clinical presentation, diagnosis, and antimicrobial treatment
Post-endocarditis clinical course and symptom recurrence leading to re-evaluation
Physical examination findings and initial hemodynamic assessment

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology of Prosthetic Valve Deterioration and Endocarditis
sections.description: This section provides the foundational knowledge needed to understand why this patient developed progressive prosthetic valve dysfunction. It covers structural valve deterioration mechanisms, the pathophysiology of prosthetic valve endocarditis, and how infection and mechanical factors contributed to severe restenosis in a multi-valve configuration.
subtopics: Structural valve deterioration: definition, timeline, and mechanisms in bioprosthetic valves
Prosthetic valve endocarditis: epidemiology, pathogenesis, and Enterococcus faecalis as a causative organism
Interaction between endocarditis and prosthetic valve structural failure: leaflet injury, fibrosis, and mechanical restriction
Characteristics of different transcatheter valve designs (Lotus, Evolut, Acurate neo2) and their implications for durability and reintervention
Hemodynamic consequences of prosthetic valve stenosis and regurgitation
Challenges of valve-in-valve procedures: effective orifice area reduction and prosthesis-patient mismatch

sections.description: This section details the comprehensive diagnostic evaluation performed to assess prosthetic valve dysfunction, confirm resolution of endocarditis, and determine feasibility of a third transcatheter intervention. It emphasizes the critical role of multimodality imaging, particularly CT, in procedural planning.
subtopics: Echocardiographic assessment: transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography for evaluating prosthetic valve function and excluding active endocarditis
Hemodynamic parameters: mean transvalvular gradients, aortic valve area calculation, and Doppler velocity index interpretation
Multislice CT for procedural planning: measuring annular dimensions, assessing valve frame geometry, and evaluating neoskirt formation
Coronary obstruction risk assessment: coronary ostial height, sinus of Valsalva dimensions, and valve-to-coronary distance measurements
Evaluation of triple-stented anatomy: frame interaction analysis and landing zone assessment
Surgical risk stratification: EuroSCORE II calculation and assessment of comorbidities precluding open surgery

sections.description: This section explains the clinical reasoning and technical considerations that guided the TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV procedure. It covers valve selection rationale, specific technical maneuvers to optimize outcomes, and the step-by-step execution of the intervention.
subtopics: Multidisciplinary heart team decision-making in complex structural heart disease
Valve selection rationale: why Acurate neo2 was chosen—supra-annular design, low frame height, and commissural alignment capabilities
High implantation strategy: rationale for implanting at the Evolut valve leaflet level to optimize effective orifice area
Commissural alignment: technique and importance for preserving future coronary access
Step-by-step procedural description: vascular access, balloon pre-dilation, valve deployment, and post-dilation
Intra-procedural monitoring: aortography, coronary flow assessment, and immediate hemodynamic evaluation
Management of prosthesis-patient mismatch in the context of triple-valve configuration

sections.description: This section presents the clinical outcomes at multiple time points, discusses the interpretation of post-procedural findings including early gradients and prosthesis-patient mismatch, and explores broader implications for lifetime management of structural valve disease.
subtopics: Immediate post-procedural results: hemodynamic parameters, valve function, and initial gradient interpretation
Hemodynamic improvement trajectory: resolution of early high gradients over follow-up, left ventricular remodeling
One-year clinical outcomes: symptom status, functional capacity, and durability of valve function
Recognition and management of prosthesis-patient mismatch in valve-in-valve procedures
Surveillance strategies for patients with multiple transcatheter valves: imaging protocols and clinical monitoring
Lifetime management principles: considerations at initial TAVI for future reintervention feasibility
Future options if current prosthesis fails: surgical explantation challenges, emerging catheter-based techniques
